﴿So travel with My servants﴾: there is an omission in the speech, meaning: take retribution upon them. Then God said to him: "Travel with My servants," and they are the Children of Israel and whoever among the Copts believed in him. Al-Zamakhsharī said: In it there are two aspects: the implied saying after the fāʾ, so that it is "He said: Travel with My servants," and that it is the answer to an omitted condition, as if it were said: "He said: If the matter is as you say, then travel with My servants." End of quote. This man often permits omitting the conditional clause and keeping its answer, which is not permitted except with clear evidence, such as the imperative preceding it or something similar, as mentioned in grammar, with disagreement on that.

﴿Indeed, you will be pursued﴾: meaning Pharaoh and his soldiers will pursue you, so you will be saved and the pursuers will drown.

﴿And leave the sea parted (rahwan)﴾: Ibn ʿAbbās said: still, as it was when it was parted. Mujāhid and ʿIkrimah said: dry, from His saying: ﴿So strike for them a dry path through the sea﴾ [Ṭāhā: 77]. al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: soft and smooth. ʿIkrimah said: with paths. Ibn Zayd said: easy. Mujāhid also said: separated. Qatādah said: Moses wanted to strike the sea with his staff, after he had crossed it, so that it would close back, and he feared that Pharaoh would follow him. It was said to him: "Why is this?" ﴿Indeed, they are an army to be drowned﴾: meaning in it, because when they see it still in its state when Moses and the Children of Israel entered it, or open as a dry path, they enter it, and God closes it upon them.

﴿How much they left behind﴾: meaning many things they left behind.

﴿Of gardens and springs﴾: their explanations were already mentioned in al-Shuʿarāʾ. Al-Jumhūr read wa-maqāmin (with a fatḥah on the mīm). Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Ibn Jubayr said: it means the place of standing (al-maqām). Ibn Hurmuz, Qatādah, Ibn al-Sumayfaʿ, and Nāfiʿ, in the narration of Kharijah, read it with a ḍammah. Qatādah said: it means the fine places of gatherings, dwellings, and others. Wa-naʿmatin (with a fatḥah on the nūn): the freshness of life and the sweetness of living. Abū Raja' read wa-naʿmatin in the accusative, conjoined to kam (how much): ﴿they were in it enjoying (fākihīn)﴾. Al-Jumhūr read it with an alif, meaning: those with contented souls and possessors of fruit, like Lābin and Tāmir. Abū Raja' and al-Ḥasan read it without an alif. The word fakih is often used for one who is light-hearted and mocking, so it is as if they were being frivolous about the form of the blessing they were in. Al-Jawharī said: "faki­ha al-rajulu" (with a kasrah) means he is faki­h if he is a joker, and fakih also means insolent. Al-Qushayrī said: fākihīn means heedless in the same way. Al-Zajjāj said: The meaning is that the matter is thus; so one stops at "thus" (kadhālika). The kāf is in the position of the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject. It was said: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, meaning: He does a deed like that to whoever He wants to destroy. Al-Kalbī said: Thus do I do to whoever disobeys Me. Al-Ḥawfī said: We destroyed with destruction, and We took retribution with retribution, thus. Al-Zamakhsharī said: The kāf is in the accusative, meaning: like that removal, We removed them from it, ﴿and We made it an inheritance for another people﴾, who were not of them, and they are the Children of Israel. They had been enslaved in the hands of the Copts, so God destroyed the Copts at their hands and made them inherit their kingdom. Qatādah and al-Ḥasan said: the Children of Israel returned to Egypt after the destruction of Pharaoh. The view of Qatādah was judged weak, because it is not reported in the well-known histories that the Children of Israel returned to Egypt at any time from that period, nor did they ever rule it, unless Qatādah meant that they inherited its type in the lands of Syria. End of quote. But there is no weight in histories, for falsehood is abundant in them, and the speech of God is truth. He said in the sura of al-Shuʿarāʾ: ﴿Thus, and We made it an inheritance for the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 59]. It was also said: "another people" refers to those who ruled Egypt after the Copts, from other than the Children of Israel.

﴿So the heaven and earth did not weep over them﴾: this is a metaphor (istiʿārah) to belittle their affair, and that nothing changed due to their destruction. In exaltation one says: the heaven and earth wept over him, the wind wept for him, and the sun darkened for him. Zayd ibn Mufarrigh said:

The wind weeps for his grief, and the lightning flashes in its clouds.

Jarīr said:

The sun is rising, not eclipsed, weeping for you, and the stars of night and the moon.

al-Nābighah said:

Ḥārith al-Jawlān wept for the loss of his lord, and Ḥawrān, humble and bowed down, is with him.

Jarīr said:

When the pride came, the walls of the city were humbled, and the high mountains.

ويَقُولُ في التَّحْقِيرِ: ماتَ فُلانٌ، فَما خَشَعَتِ الجِبالُ.

It is said, in belittling someone: "So-and-so died, and the mountains did not humble themselves."

ونِسْبَةُ هَذِهِ الأشْياءِ لِما لا يَعْقِلُ ولا يَصِيرُ ذَلِكَ مِنهُ حَقِيقَةً، عِبارَةٌ عَنْ تَأثُّرِ النّاسِ لَهُ، أوْ عَنْ عَدَمِهِ.

Attributing these things to what has no intellect, and such (acts) not truly arising from it, is an expression of the people's being affected by him, or of their not being affected.

وقِيلَ: هو عَلى حَذْفِ مُضافٍ، أيْ: فَما بَكى عَلَيْهِمْ أهْلُ السَّماءِ وأهْلُ المَلائِكَةِ وأهْلُ الأرْضِ، وهُمُ المُؤْمِنُونَ، بَلْ كانُوا بِهَلاكِهِمْ مَسْرُورِينَ.

It has also been said that it involves an elided noun (ḥadhf muḍāf), meaning: "The people of the heavens, the people of the angels and the people of the earth did not weep over them," and they are the believers; rather, they were delighted at their destruction. This was narrated from al-Ḥasan.

وما رُوِيَ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، وابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، ومُجاهِدٍ، وابْنِ جُبَيْرٍ: إنَّ المُؤْمِنَ إذا ماتَ، بَكى عَلَيْهِ مِنَ (p-٣٧)الأرْضِ مَوْضِعُ عِبادَتِهِ أرْبَعِينَ صَباحًا، وبَكى عَلَيْهِ في السَّماءِ مَوْضِعُ صُعُودِ عَمَلِهِ. قالُوا: فَلَمْ يَكُنْ في قَوْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ مَن هَذِهِ حالُهُ تَمْثِيلٌ.

What was narrated from ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and Ibn Jubayr is that when a believer dies, the place of his worship on the earth weeps for him for forty mornings, and in the heavens the place where his deeds ascended weeps for him. They said: "Thus there was none among the people of Pharaoh whose state was this," as an illustration.

﴿وما كانُوا مُنْظَرِينَ﴾: أيْ مُؤَخَّرِينَ عَنِ العَذابِ لَمّا حانَ وقْتُ هَلاكِهِمْ، بَلْ عَجَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهم ذَلِكَ في الدُّنْيا.

﴿And they were not reprieved﴾: that is, they were not delayed from the punishment when the time of their destruction had come; rather, God hastened that for them in this world.

﴿So watch for the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke﴾. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd al-Khudrī, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and al-Ḥasan said: It is a smoke that will come on the Day of Resurrection. It will afflict the believer with something like a cold, and it will cook the heads of the disbelievers and the hypocrites, until they become like a roasted, grilled meat (miṣlaqah ḥanīdhah).

Ibn Masʿūd, Abū al-ʿĀliyah, and al-Nakhaʿī said: It is the smoke that Quraysh saw. It was said to ʿAbdullāh (Ibn Masʿūd): "A storyteller at the gates of Kinda says that it is a smoke that will come on the Day of Resurrection and will seize the breaths of the people." He said: "Whoever knows something should speak of it, and whoever does not know should say: God knows best. Now, I will tell you that when Quraysh rebelled against the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he invoked against them, saying: 'O God, tighten Your grip upon Mudar, and make it upon them years like the years of Joseph.' So hardship struck them until they ate carrion and al-ʿilhiz. Al-ʿilhiz is wool in which a tick falls, and the wool is roasted with the blood of the tick and eaten." In the same narration: "Until they ate the bones." A man would see smoke between the sky and the earth, and a man would speak with another and hear his words but would not see him because of the smoke. Abū Sufyān and a group with him came to him (the Prophet, ﷺ), appealed to him by God and by the ties of kinship, and promised him that if he prayed for them and lifted it from them, they would believe. When he lifted it from them, they returned to their polytheism. In the same narration: The Prophet (ﷺ) had mercy on them and sent them charity and property. Also in it: When prosperity reached them, they returned to their former state, and God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿On the Day when We will seize with the greatest seizing, indeed We will take retribution﴾. He said: This means the Day of Badr.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Five have already passed: the smoke, the lazām, the seizing, the moon, and the Romans. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj said: ﴿The Day when the sky will bring forth﴾ is the Day of the Conquest of Mecca, when the dust covered the sky.

In the narration of Ḥudhayfah: The first of the signs are the emergence of the Dajjāl (the false messiah), the smoke, the descent of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, and a fire that will come out from the depth of ʿAdan. In it I said: "O Prophet of God, what is the smoke regarding this verse: ﴿So watch for the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke﴾?" He mentioned the rest of the narration, and we have summarized it.

﴿A visible smoke﴾: clearly visible. There is no doubt that it is a smoke. ﴿Covering the people﴾: it encompasses them. If it is the one Quraysh saw, then "the people" is specific to the disbelievers of Mecca, and it has already passed, as Ibn Masʿūd said. If it is among the minor signs of the Hour, or it is the Day of Resurrection, then "the people" is general to those who encounter the time of the signs, and general to all people on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿This is a painful punishment﴾ up to ﴿believers﴾ is in a position of accusative (naṣb, the grammatical case of the object) by a verb of saying that is omitted, and it is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: they will say. It is permissible that it be a report from God, as if it were an expression of amazement, as He said in the story of the sacrificed son: ﴿Indeed, this is a manifest trial﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 106].

﴿Indeed, we are believers﴾: a promise of faith if the punishment is lifted from them, and faith is obligatory whether the punishment is lifted or not.

﴿How can they have the reminder?﴾: that is, how can they be mindful, take admonition, and say what they promised of faith at the lifting of the punishment, when there has come to them what is greater? And it is included in the category of "being mindful through the lifting of the smoke"? That is what appeared at the hand of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) of signs and clear proofs, of the inimitable Book and other miracles. Yet they were not mindful, turned away from it, and slandered him by claiming that ʿAddās, a non-Arab slave of a man from Thaqīf, was the one who taught him, and they attributed him to madness. Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh recited: muʿallimun (with a kasra on the lām).

﴿Indeed, We will lift the punishment a little﴾: a report about the establishment of the proof against them, and an emphasis on granting them respite. Then He informed that they would return to disbelief. Qatādah said: It is a threat of the return in the Hereafter. If the address is to Quraysh when the drought struck them, it is clear. If the smoke is before the Day of Resurrection, then when the sky brings the punishment, their hypocrites and disbelievers will beseech and say: "Our Lord, lift the punishment from us; indeed we are believers." So He lifts it from them; it was said: after forty days. When He lifts it from them, they will apostatize. According to this view, the Day of the Great Seizing is the Day of Resurrection, like His saying: ﴿So when the Greatest Calamity comes﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 34]. That it is the Day of Resurrection is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Qatādah. That it is the Day of Badr is the view of ʿAbdullāh, Ubayy, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Mujāhid.

The word yawma (the object of time) in ﴿the Day We will seize﴾ is in the accusative. It was said: it is governed by their remembrance (dhikrāhum). It was said: it is governed by ﴿We will take retribution﴾, which indicates it. This was judged weak because the accusative is only governed by a verb. It was also said: it is governed by "will take retribution," and this was rebutted on the grounds that what follows inna does not govern what precedes it. Al-Jumhūr (the majority) recited nabṭishu, with a fatḥah on the nūn and a kasrah on the ṭāʾ. Al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar read it with a ḍammah on it; also al-Ḥasan, Abū Raja', and Ṭalḥah read it with a ḍammah on the nūn and a kasrah on the ṭāʾ, meaning: We will empower over them one who seizes them. The word al-baṭshata (the seizing), in this reading, is not in the accusative governed by nabṭishu, but by an implied verb, meaning: We will make that empowered one seize the seizing; or al-baṭshata means the same as al-ibṭāshah (the act of seizing), so it is in the accusative governed by nabṭishu.

﴿And We had already tested before them the people of Pharaoh﴾: this is like an example for Quraysh. The story of the one to whom Moses, peace be upon him, was sent is mentioned, and they denied him, so God destroyed them. It was also read fattannā, with a shaddah on the tāʾ, for emphasis in the verb or for multiplication, related to ... ﴿And there came to them a noble messenger﴾: meaning noble with God and with the believers, said by al-Farrāʾ; or noble in himself, because prophets are only sent from the best of people, said by Abū Sulaymān; or noble in character, good of disposition, said by Muqātil.

﴿That deliver to me the servants of God﴾: it may be that anna is explanatory (tafsīriyyah), since something preceded that indicates the meaning of saying, which is "a noble messenger." It may also be that anna is the lightened form (mukhaffafah) of the heavy (thaqīlah) anna, or the anna that governs the present verb (nāṣibah), since it is connected to the imperative. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Deliver to me obedience, O servants of God," meaning: follow me in what I call you to of faith. Mujāhid, Qatādah, and Ibn Zayd said: He asked them to deliver to him the Children of Israel, as He said: ﴿So send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them﴾ [Ṭāhā: 47]. According to the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿibāda llāh (servants of God) is a vocative, and the object of "deliver" is omitted. According to the view of Mujāhid and those mentioned with him, ʿibāda llāh is the object of "deliver."

﴿Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you﴾: meaning not accused, God has entrusted me with His revelation and His message.

﴿And that you not exalt yourselves over God﴾: meaning do not be arrogant against the worship of God, said by Yaḥyā ibn Sallām. Ibn Jurayj said: Do not magnify yourselves over God. It was said: the difference between them is that magnification (taʿẓīm) is the superiority of the powerful, and arrogance (istikbār) is the elevation of one who is despised, mentioned by al-Māwardī. And anna here had the preceding one in its three aspects.

﴿Indeed, I bring you a clear authority﴾: meaning a clear proof in itself, and making clear the truth of my claim. Al-Jumhūr read innī with a kasrah on the hamzah, as a report. A group read it with a fatḥah on the hamzah. The meaning then: "Do not exalt yourselves over God because I come to you," so this is a rebuke to them, as you would say: "Do you become angry if someone tells you the truth?"

﴿And indeed, I have sought refuge﴾: meaning I have sought protection ﴿with my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me﴾. They had threatened him with death, so he sought refuge from that. It was read ʿudtu (with the vowel of the verb), with idghām (assimilation of the two identical letters). Qatādah and others said: The stoning here is with stones. Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Ṣāliḥ said: with insult. Qatādah's view is more evident, because words not befitting were said against him. This seeking of refuge was before God informed him with His saying: ﴿They will not reach you﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 35].

﴿And if you do not believe in me﴾, meaning you do not affirm me, ﴿then leave me alone﴾, meaning be apart from me. This is a good form of partnership (mushārakah), ﴿So he called upon his Lord: "Indeed, I am overpowered, so give victory"﴾ [al-Qamar: 10].

﴿That these people﴾: a word of contempt for them. Al-Jumhūr read anna hāʾulāʾi with a fatḥah on the hamzah, meaning: because these people. Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿĪsā, al-Ḥasan in one narration, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it with a kasrah.

﴿So travel with My servants﴾: there is an omission in the speech, meaning: take retribution upon them. Then God said to him: "Travel with My servants," and they are the Children of Israel and whoever among the Copts believed in him. Al-Zamakhsharī said: In it there are two aspects: the implied saying after the fāʾ, so that it is "He said: Travel with My servants," and that it is the answer to an omitted condition, as if it were said: "He said: If the matter is as you say, then travel with My servants." End of quote. ﴿Indeed, you will be pursued﴾: meaning Pharaoh and his soldiers will pursue you, so you will be saved and the pursuers will drown.

﴿And leave the sea parted (rahwan)﴾: Ibn ʿAbbās said: still, as it was when it was parted. Mujāhid and ʿIkrimah said: dry, from His saying: ﴿So strike for them a dry path through the sea﴾ [Ṭāhā: 77]. al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: soft and smooth. ʿIkrimah said: with paths. Ibn Zayd said: easy. It was also said: "another people" refers to those who ruled Egypt after the Copts, from other than the Children of Israel.

﴿So the heaven and earth did not weep over them﴾: this is a metaphor (istiʿārah) to belittle their affair, and that nothing changed due to their destruction. In exaltation one says: the heaven and earth wept over him, the wind wept for him, and the sun darkened for him. Zayd ibn Mufarrigh said:

What was narrated from ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and Ibn Jubayr is that when a believer dies, the place of his worship on the earth weeps for him for forty mornings, and in the heavens the place where his deeds ascended weeps for him. They said: "Thus there was none among the people of Pharaoh whose state was this," as an illustration.

﴿وما كانُوا مُنْظَرِينَ﴾: أيْ مُؤَخَّرِينَ عَنِ العَذابِ لَمّا حانَ وقْتُ هَلاكِهِمْ، بَلْ عَجَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهم ذَلِكَ في الدُّنْيا.

﴿And they were not reprieved﴾: that is, they were not delayed from the punishment when the time of their destruction had come; rather, God hastened that for them in this world.

﴿So watch for the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke﴾. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd al-Khudrī, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and al-Ḥasan said: It is a smoke that will come on the Day of Resurrection. It will afflict the believer with something like a cold, and it will cook the heads of the disbelievers and the hypocrites, until they become like a roasted, grilled meat (miṣlaqah ḥanīdhah).

Ibn Masʿūd, Abū al-ʿĀliyah, and al-Nakhaʿī said: It is the smoke that Quraysh saw. It was said to ʿAbdullāh (Ibn Masʿūd): "A storyteller at the gates of Kinda says that it is a smoke that will come on the Day of Resurrection and will seize the breaths of the people." He said: "Whoever knows something should speak of it, and whoever does not know should say: God knows best. Now, I will tell you that when Quraysh rebelled against the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he invoked against them, saying: 'O God, tighten Your grip upon Mudar, and make it upon them years like the years of Joseph.' So hardship struck them until they ate carrion and al-ʿilhiz. Al-ʿilhiz is wool in which a tick falls, and the wool is roasted with the blood of the tick and eaten." In the same narration: "Until they ate the bones." A man would see smoke between the sky and the earth, and a man would speak with another and hear his words but would not see him because of the smoke. Abū Sufyān and a group with him came to him (the Prophet, ﷺ), appealed to him by God and by the ties of kinship, and promised him that if he prayed for them and lifted it from them, they would believe. When he lifted it from them, they returned to their polytheism. In the same narration: The Prophet (ﷺ) had mercy on them and sent them charity and property. Also in it: When prosperity reached them, they returned to their former state, and God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿On the Day when We will seize with the greatest seizing, indeed We will take retribution﴾. He said: This means the Day of Badr.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Five have already passed: the smoke, the lazām, the seizing, the moon, and the Romans. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj said: ﴿The Day when the sky will bring forth﴾ is the Day of the Conquest of Mecca, when the dust covered the sky.

In the narration of Ḥudhayfah: The first of the signs are the emergence of the Dajjāl (the false messiah), the smoke, the descent of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, and a fire that will come out from the depth of ʿAdan. In it I said: "O Prophet of God, what is the smoke regarding this verse: ﴿So watch for the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke﴾?" He mentioned the rest of the narration, and we have summarized it.

﴿A visible smoke﴾: clearly visible. There is no doubt that it is a smoke. ﴿Covering the people﴾: it encompasses them. If it is the one Quraysh saw, then "the people" is specific to the disbelievers of Mecca, and it has already passed, as Ibn Masʿūd said. If it is among the minor signs of the Hour, or it is the Day of Resurrection, then "the people" is general to those who encounter the time of the signs, and general to all people on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿This is a painful punishment﴾ up to ﴿believers﴾ is in a position of accusative (naṣb, the grammatical case of the object) by a verb of saying that is omitted, and it is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: they will say. It is permissible that it be a report from God, as if it were an expression of amazement, as He said in the story of the sacrificed son: ﴿Indeed, this is a manifest trial﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 106].

﴿Indeed, we are believers﴾: a promise of faith if the punishment is lifted from them, and faith is obligatory whether the punishment is lifted or not.

﴿How can they have the reminder?﴾: that is, how can they be mindful, take admonition, and say what they promised of faith at the lifting of the punishment, when there has come to them what is greater? And it is included in the category of "being mindful through the lifting of the smoke"? That is what appeared at the hand of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) of signs and clear proofs, of the inimitable Book and other miracles. Yet they were not mindful, turned away from it, and slandered him by claiming that ʿAddās, a non-Arab slave of a man from Thaqīf, was the one who taught him, and they attributed him to madness. Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh recited: muʿallimun (with a kasra on the lām).

﴿Indeed, We will lift the punishment a little﴾: a report about the establishment of the proof against them, and an emphasis on granting them respite. Then He informed that they would return to disbelief. Qatādah said: It is a threat of the return in the Hereafter. If the address is to Quraysh when the drought struck them, it is clear. If the smoke is before the Day of Resurrection, then when the sky brings the punishment, their hypocrites and disbelievers will beseech and say: "Our Lord, lift the punishment from us; indeed we are believers." So He lifts it from them; it was said: after forty days. When He lifts it from them, they will apostatize. According to this view, the Day of the Great Seizing is the Day of Resurrection, like His saying: ﴿So when the Greatest Calamity comes﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 34]. That it is the Day of Resurrection is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Qatādah. That it is the Day of Badr is the view of ʿAbdullāh, Ubayy, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Mujāhid.

The word yawma (the object of time) in ﴿the Day We will seize﴾ is in the accusative. It was said: it is governed by their remembrance (dhikrāhum). It was said: it is governed by ﴿We will take retribution﴾, which indicates it. This was judged weak because the accusative is only governed by a verb. It was also said: it is governed by "will take retribution," and this was rebutted on the grounds that what follows inna does not govern what precedes it. Al-Jumhūr (the majority) recited nabṭishu, with a fatḥah on the nūn and a kasrah on the ṭāʾ. Al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar read it with a ḍammah on it; also al-Ḥasan, Abū Raja', and Ṭalḥah read it with a ḍammah on the nūn and a kasrah on the ṭāʾ, meaning: We will empower over them one who seizes them. The word al-baṭshata (the seizing), in this reading, is not in the accusative governed by nabṭishu, but by an implied verb, meaning: We will make that empowered one seize the seizing; or al-baṭshata means the same as al-ibṭāshah (the act of seizing), so it is in the accusative governed by nabṭishu.

﴿And We had already tested before them the people of Pharaoh﴾: this is like an example for Quraysh. The story of the one to whom Moses, peace be upon him, was sent is mentioned, and they denied him, so God destroyed them. It was also read fattannā, with a shaddah on the tāʾ, for emphasis in the verb or for multiplication, related to ... ﴿And there came to them a noble messenger﴾: meaning noble with God and with the believers, said by al-Farrāʾ; or noble in himself, because prophets are only sent from the best of people, said by Abū Sulaymān; or noble in character, good of disposition, said by Muqātil.

﴿That deliver to me the servants of God﴾: it may be that anna is explanatory (tafsīriyyah), since something preceded that indicates the meaning of saying, which is "a noble messenger." It may also be that anna is the lightened form (mukhaffafah) of the heavy (thaqīlah) anna, or the anna that governs the present verb (nāṣibah), since it is connected to the imperative. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Deliver to me obedience, O servants of God," meaning: follow me in what I call you to of faith. Mujāhid, Qatādah, and Ibn Zayd said: He asked them to deliver to him the Children of Israel, as He said: ﴿So send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them﴾ [Ṭāhā: 47]. According to the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿibāda llāh (servants of God) is a vocative, and the object of "deliver" is omitted. According to the view of Mujāhid and those mentioned with him, ʿibāda llāh is the object of "deliver."

﴿Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you﴾: meaning not accused, God has entrusted me with His revelation and His message.

﴿And that you not exalt yourselves over God﴾: meaning do not be arrogant against the worship of God, said by Yaḥyā ibn Sallām. Ibn Jurayj said: Do not magnify yourselves over God. It was said: the difference between them is that magnification (taʿẓīm) is the superiority of the powerful, and arrogance (istikbār) is the elevation of one who is despised, mentioned by al-Māwardī. And anna here had the preceding one in its three aspects.

﴿Indeed, I bring you a clear authority﴾: meaning a clear proof in itself, and making clear the truth of my claim. Al-Jumhūr read innī with a kasrah on the hamzah, as a report. A group read it with a fatḥah on the hamzah. The meaning then: "Do not exalt yourselves over God because I come to you," so this is a rebuke to them, as you would say: "Do you become angry if someone tells you the truth?"

﴿And indeed, I have sought refuge﴾: meaning I have sought protection ﴿with my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me﴾. They had threatened him with death, so he sought refuge from that. It was read ʿudtu (with the vowel of the verb), with idghām (assimilation of the two identical letters). Qatādah and others said: The stoning here is with stones. Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Ṣāliḥ said: with insult. Qatādah's view is more evident, because words not befitting were said against him. This seeking of refuge was before God informed him with His saying: ﴿They will not reach you﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 35].

﴿And if you do not believe in me﴾, meaning you do not affirm me, ﴿then leave me alone﴾, meaning be apart from me. This is a good form of partnership (mushārakah), ﴿So he called upon his Lord: "Indeed, I am overpowered, so give victory"﴾ [al-Qamar: 10].

﴿That these people﴾: a word of contempt for them. Al-Jumhūr read anna hāʾulāʾi with a fatḥah on the hamzah, meaning: because these people. Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿĪsā, al-Ḥasan in one narration, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it with a kasrah.

﴿So travel with My servants﴾: there is an omission in the speech, meaning: take retribution upon them. Then God said to him: "Travel with My servants," and they are the Children of Israel and whoever among the Copts believed in him. Al-Zamakhsharī said: In it there are two aspects: the implied saying after the fāʾ, so that it is "He said: Travel with My servants," and that it is the answer to an omitted condition, as if it were said: "He said: If the matter is as you say, then travel with My servants." End of quote. This man often permits omitting the conditional clause and keeping its answer, which is not permitted except with clear evidence, such as the imperative preceding it or something similar, as mentioned in grammar, with disagreement on that.

﴿Indeed, you will be pursued﴾: meaning Pharaoh and his soldiers will pursue you, so you will be saved and the pursuers will drown.

﴿And leave the sea parted (rahwan)﴾: Ibn ʿAbbās said: still, as it was when it was parted. Mujāhid and ʿIkrimah said: dry, from His saying: ﴿So strike for them a dry path through the sea﴾ [Ṭāhā: 77]. al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: soft and smooth. ʿIkrimah said: with paths. Ibn Zayd said: easy. Mujāhid also said: separated. Qatādah said: Moses wanted to strike the sea with his staff, after he had crossed it, so that it would close back, and he feared that Pharaoh would follow him. It was said to him: "Why is this?" ﴿Indeed, they are an army to be drowned﴾: meaning in it, because when they see it still in its state when Moses and the Children of Israel entered it, or open as a dry path, they enter it, and God closes it upon them.

﴿How much they left behind﴾: meaning many things they left behind.

﴿Of gardens and springs﴾: their explanations were already mentioned in al-Shuʿarāʾ. Al-Jumhūr read wa-maqāmin (with a fatḥah on the mīm). Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Ibn Jubayr said: it means the place of standing (al-maqām). Ibn Hurmuz, Qatādah, Ibn al-Sumayfaʿ, and Nāfiʿ, in the narration of Kharijah, read it with a ḍammah. Qatādah said: it means the fine places of gatherings, dwellings, and others. Wa-naʿmatin (with a fatḥah on the nūn): the freshness of life and the sweetness of living. Abū Raja' read wa-naʿmatin in the accusative, conjoined to kam (how much): ﴿they were in it enjoying (fākihīn)﴾. Al-Jumhūr read it with an alif, meaning: those with contented souls and possessors of fruit, like Lābin and Tāmir. Abū Raja' and al-Ḥasan read it without an alif. The word fakih is often used for one who is light-hearted and mocking, so it is as if they were being frivolous about the form of the blessing they were in. Al-Jawharī said: "faki­ha al-rajulu" (with a kasrah) means he is faki­h if he is a joker, and fakih also means insolent. Al-Qushayrī said: fākihīn means heedless in the same way. Al-Zajjāj said: The meaning is that the matter is thus; so one stops at "thus" (kadhālika). The kāf is in the position of the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject. It was said: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, meaning: He does a deed like that to whoever He wants to destroy. Al-Kalbī said: Thus do I do to whoever disobeys Me. Al-Ḥawfī said: We destroyed with destruction, and We took retribution with retribution, thus. Al-Zamakhsharī said: The kāf is in the accusative, meaning: like that removal, We removed them from it, ﴿and We made it an inheritance for another people﴾, who were not of them, and they are the Children of Israel. They had been enslaved in the hands of the Copts, so God destroyed the Copts at their hands and made them inherit their kingdom. Qatādah and al-Ḥasan said: the Children of Israel returned to Egypt after the destruction of Pharaoh. The view of Qatādah was judged weak, because it is not reported in the well-known histories that the Children of Israel returned to Egypt at any time from that period, nor did they ever rule it, unless Qatādah meant that they inherited its type in the lands of Syria. End of quote. But there is no weight in histories, for falsehood is abundant in them, and the speech of God is truth. He said in the sura of al-Shuʿarāʾ: ﴿Thus, and We made it an inheritance for the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 59]. It was also said: "another people" refers to those who ruled Egypt after the Copts, from other than the Children of Israel.

﴿So the heaven and earth did not weep over them﴾: this is a metaphor (istiʿārah) to belittle their affair, and that nothing changed due to their destruction. In exaltation one says: the heaven and earth wept over him, the wind wept for him, and the sun darkened for him. Zayd ibn Mufarrigh said:

The wind weeps for his grief, and the lightning flashes in its clouds.

Jarīr said:

The sun is rising, not eclipsed, weeping for you, and the stars of night and the moon.

al-Nābighah said:

Ḥārith al-Jawlān wept for the loss of his lord, and Ḥawrān, humble and bowed down, is with him.

Jarīr said:

When the pride came, the walls of the city were humbled, and the high mountains.

ويَقُولُ في التَّحْقِيرِ: ماتَ فُلانٌ، فَما خَشَعَتِ الجِبالُ.

It is said, in belittling someone: "So-and-so died, and the mountains did not humble themselves."

ونِسْبَةُ هَذِهِ الأشْياءِ لِما لا يَعْقِلُ ولا يَصِيرُ ذَلِكَ مِنهُ حَقِيقَةً، عِبارَةٌ عَنْ تَأثُّرِ النّاسِ لَهُ، أوْ عَنْ عَدَمِهِ.

Attributing these things to what has no intellect, and such (acts) not truly arising from it, is an expression of the people's being affected by him, or of their not being affected.

وقِيلَ: هو عَلى حَذْفِ مُضافٍ، أيْ: فَما بَكى عَلَيْهِمْ أهْلُ السَّماءِ وأهْلُ المَلائِكَةِ وأهْلُ الأرْضِ، وهُمُ المُؤْمِنُونَ، بَلْ كانُوا بِهَلاكِهِمْ مَسْرُورِينَ.

It was also said: it is governed by "will take retribution," and this was rebutted on the grounds that what follows inna does not govern what precedes it. Al-Jumhūr (the majority) recited nabṭishu, with a fatḥah on the nūn and a kasrah on the ṭāʾ. Al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar read it with a ḍammah on it; also al-Ḥasan, Abū Raja', and Ṭalḥah read it with a ḍammah on the nūn and a kasrah on the ṭāʾ, meaning: We will empower over them one who seizes them. The word al-baṭshata (the seizing), in this reading, is not in the accusative governed by nabṭishu, but by an implied verb, meaning: We will make that empowered one seize the seizing; or al-baṭshata means the same as al-ibṭāshah (the act of seizing), so it is in the accusative governed by nabṭishu.

﴿And We had already tested before them the people of Pharaoh﴾: this is like an example for Quraysh. The story of the one to whom Moses, peace be upon him, was sent is mentioned, and they denied him, so God destroyed them. It was also read fattannā, with a shaddah on the tāʾ, for emphasis in the verb or for multiplication, related to ... ﴿And there came to them a noble messenger﴾: meaning noble with God and with the believers, said by al-Farrāʾ; or noble in himself, because prophets are only sent from the best of people, said by Abū Sulaymān; or noble in character, good of disposition, said by Muqātil.

﴿That deliver to me the servants of God﴾: it may be that anna is explanatory (tafsīriyyah), since something preceded that indicates the meaning of saying, which is "a noble messenger." It may also be that anna is the lightened form (mukhaffafah) of the heavy (thaqīlah) anna, or the anna that governs the present verb (nāṣibah), since it is connected to the imperative. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Deliver to me obedience, O servants of God," meaning: follow me in what I call you to of faith. Mujāhid, Qatādah, and Ibn Zayd said: He asked them to deliver to him the Children of Israel, as He said: ﴿So send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them﴾ [Ṭāhā: 47]. According to the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿibāda llāh (servants of God) is a vocative, and the object of "deliver" is omitted. According to the view of Mujāhid and those mentioned with him, ʿibāda llāh is the object of "deliver."

﴿Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you﴾: meaning not accused, God has entrusted me with His revelation and His message.

﴿And that you not exalt yourselves over God﴾: meaning do not be arrogant against the worship of God, said by Yaḥyā ibn Sallām. Ibn Jurayj said: Do not magnify yourselves over God. It was said: the difference between them is that magnification (taʿẓīm) is the superiority of the powerful, and arrogance (istikbār) is the elevation of one who is despised, mentioned by al-Māwardī. And anna here had the preceding one in its three aspects.

﴿Indeed, I bring you a clear authority﴾: meaning a clear proof in itself, and making clear the truth of my claim. Al-Jumhūr read innī with a kasrah on the hamzah, as a report. A group read it with a fatḥah on the hamzah. The meaning then: "Do not exalt yourselves over God because I come to you," so this is a rebuke to them, as you would say: "Do you become angry if someone tells you the truth?"

﴿And indeed, I have sought refuge﴾: meaning I have sought protection ﴿with my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me﴾. They had threatened him with death, so he sought refuge from that. It was read ʿudtu (with the vowel of the verb), with idghām (assimilation of the two identical letters). Qatādah and others said: The stoning here is with stones. Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Ṣāliḥ said: with insult. Qatādah's view is more evident, because words not befitting were said against him. This seeking of refuge was before God informed him with His saying: ﴿They will not reach you﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 35].

﴿And if you do not believe in me﴾, meaning you do not affirm me, ﴿then leave me alone﴾, meaning be apart from me. This is a good form of partnership (mushārakah), ﴿So he called upon his Lord: "Indeed, I am overpowered, so give victory"﴾ [al-Qamar: 10].

﴿That these people﴾: a word of contempt for them. Al-Jumhūr read anna hāʾulāʾi with a fatḥah on the hamzah, meaning: because these people. Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿĪsā, al-Ḥasan in one narration, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it with a kasrah.

﴿So travel with My servants﴾: there is an omission in the speech, meaning: take retribution upon them. Then God said to him: "Travel with My servants," and they are the Children of Israel and whoever among the Copts believed in him. Al-Zamakhsharī said: In it there are two aspects: the implied saying after the fāʾ, so that it is "He said: Travel with My servants," and that it is the answer to an omitted condition, as if it were said: "He said: If the matter is as you say, then travel with My servants." End of quote. This man often permits omitting the conditional clause and keeping its answer, which is not permitted except with clear evidence, such as the imperative preceding it or something similar, as mentioned in grammar, with disagreement on that.

﴿Indeed, you will be pursued﴾: meaning Pharaoh and his soldiers will pursue you, so you will be saved and the pursuers will drown.

﴿And leave the sea parted (rahwan)﴾: Ibn ʿAbbās said: still, as it was when it was parted. Mujāhid and ʿIkrimah said: dry, from His saying: ﴿So strike for them a dry path through the sea﴾ [Ṭāhā: 77]. al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: soft and smooth. ʿIkrimah said: with paths. Ibn Zayd said: easy. Mujāhid also said: separated. Qatādah said: Moses wanted to strike the sea with his staff, after he had crossed it, so that it would close back, and he feared that Pharaoh would follow him. It was said to him: "Why is this?" ﴿Indeed, they are an army to be drowned﴾: meaning in it, because when they see it still in its state when Moses and the Children of Israel entered it, or open as a dry path, they enter it, and God closes it upon them.

﴿How much they left behind﴾: meaning many things they left behind.

﴿Of gardens and springs﴾: their explanations were already mentioned in al-Shuʿarāʾ. Al-Jumhūr read wa-maqāmin (with a fatḥah on the mīm). Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Ibn Jubayr said: it means the place of standing (al-maqām). Ibn Hurmuz, Qatādah, Ibn al-Sumayfaʿ, and Nāfiʿ, in the narration of Kharijah, read it with a ḍammah. Qatādah said: it means the fine places of gatherings, dwellings, and others. Wa-naʿmatin (with a fatḥah on the nūn): the freshness of life and the sweetness of living. Abū Raja' read wa-naʿmatin in the accusative, conjoined to kam (how much): ﴿they were in it enjoying (fākihīn)﴾. Al-Jumhūr read it with an alif, meaning: those with contented souls and possessors of fruit, like Lābin and Tāmir. Abū Raja' and al-Ḥasan read it without an alif. The word fakih is often used for one who is light-hearted and mocking, so it is as if they were being frivolous about the form of the blessing they were in. Al-Jawharī said: "faki­ha al-rajulu" (with a kasrah) means he is faki­h if he is a joker, and fakih also means insolent. Al-Qushayrī said: fākihīn means heedless in the same way. Al-Zajjāj said: The meaning is that the matter is thus; so one stops at "thus" (kadhālika). The kāf is in the position of the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject. It was said: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, meaning: He does a deed like that to whoever He wants to destroy. Al-Kalbī said: Thus do I do to whoever disobeys Me. Al-Ḥawfī said: We destroyed with destruction, and We took retribution with retribution, thus. Al-Zamakhsharī said: The kāf is in the accusative, meaning: like that removal, We removed them from it, ﴿and We made it an inheritance for another people﴾, who were not of them, and they are the Children of Israel. They had been enslaved in the hands of the Copts, so God destroyed the Copts at their hands and made them inherit their kingdom. Qatādah and al-Ḥasan said: the Children of Israel returned to Egypt after the destruction of Pharaoh. The view of Qatādah was judged weak, because it is not reported in the well-known histories that the Children of Israel returned to Egypt at any time from that period, nor did they ever rule it, unless Qatādah meant that they inherited its type in the lands of Syria. End of quote. But there is no weight in histories, for falsehood is abundant in them, and the speech of God is truth. He said in the sura of al-Shuʿarāʾ: ﴿Thus, and We made it an inheritance for the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 59]. It was also said: "another people" refers to those who ruled Egypt after the Copts, from other than the Children of Israel.

﴿So the heaven and earth did not weep over them﴾: this is a metaphor (istiʿārah) to belittle their affair, and that nothing changed due to their destruction. In exaltation one says: the heaven and earth wept over him, the wind wept for him, and the sun darkened for him. Zayd ibn Mufarrigh said:

The wind weeps for his grief, and the lightning flashes in its clouds.

Jarīr said:

The sun is rising, not eclipsed, weeping for you, and the stars of night and the moon.

al-Nābighah said:

Ḥārith al-Jawlān wept for the loss of his lord, and Ḥawrān, humble and bowed down, is with him.

Jarīr said:

When the pride came, the walls of the city were humbled, and the high mountains.

ويَقُولُ في التَّحْقِيرِ: ماتَ فُلانٌ، فَما خَشَعَتِ الجِبالُ.

It is said, in belittling someone: "So-and-so died, and the mountains did not humble themselves."

ونِسْبَةُ هَذِهِ الأشْياءِ لِما لا يَعْقِلُ ولا يَصِيرُ ذَلِكَ مِنهُ حَقِيقَةً، عِبارَةٌ عَنْ تَأثُّرِ النّاسِ لَهُ، أوْ عَنْ عَدَمِهِ.

Attributing these things to what has no intellect, and such (acts) not truly arising from it, is an expression of the people's being affected by him, or of their not being affected.

وقِيلَ: هو عَلى حَذْفِ مُضافٍ، أيْ: فَما بَكى عَلَيْهِمْ أهْلُ السَّماءِ وأهْلُ المَلائِكَةِ وأهْلُ الأرْضِ، وهُمُ المُؤْمِنُونَ، بَلْ كانُوا بِهَلاكِهِمْ مَسْرُورِينَ.

It has also been said that it involves an elided noun (ḥadhf muḍāf), meaning: "The people of the heavens, the people of the angels and the people of the earth did not weep over them," and they are the believers; rather, they were delighted at their destruction. This was narrated from al-Ḥasan.

وما رُوِيَ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، وابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، ومُجاهِدٍ، وابْنِ جُبَيْرٍ: إنَّ المُؤْمِنَ إذا ماتَ، بَكى عَلَيْهِ مِنَ (p-٣٧)الأرْضِ مَوْضِعُ عِبادَتِهِ أرْبَعِينَ صَباحًا، وبَكى عَلَيْهِ في السَّماءِ مَوْضِعُ صُعُودِ عَمَلِهِ. قالُوا: فَلَمْ يَكُنْ في قَوْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ مَن هَذِهِ حالُهُ تَمْثِيلٌ.

What was narrated from ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and Ibn Jubayr is that when a believer dies, the place of his worship on the earth weeps for him for forty mornings, and in the heavens the place where his deeds ascended weeps for him. They said: "Thus there was none among the people of Pharaoh whose state was this," as an illustration.

﴿وما كانُوا مُنْظَرِينَ﴾: أيْ مُؤَخَّرِينَ عَنِ العَذابِ لَمّا حانَ وقْتُ هَلاكِهِمْ، بَلْ عَجَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهم ذَلِكَ في الدُّنْيا.

﴿And they were not reprieved﴾: that is, they were not delayed from the punishment when the time of their destruction had come; rather, God hastened that for them in this world.

﴿So watch for the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke﴾. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd al-Khudrī, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and al-Ḥasan said: It is a smoke that will come on the Day of Resurrection. It will afflict the believer with something like a cold, and it will cook the heads of the disbelievers and the hypocrites, until they become like a roasted, grilled meat (miṣlaqah ḥanīdhah).

Ibn Masʿūd, Abū al-ʿĀliyah, and al-Nakhaʿī said: It is the smoke that Quraysh saw. It was said to ʿAbdullāh (Ibn Masʿūd): "A storyteller at the gates of Kinda says that it is a smoke that will come on the Day of Resurrection and will seize the breaths of the people." He said: "Whoever knows something should speak of it, and whoever does not know should say: God knows best. Now, I will tell you that when Quraysh rebelled against the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he invoked against them, saying: 'O God, tighten Your grip upon Mudar, and make it upon them years like the years of Joseph.' So hardship struck them until they ate carrion and al-ʿilhiz. Al-ʿilhiz is wool in which a tick falls, and the wool is roasted with the blood of the tick and eaten." In the same narration: "Until they ate the bones." A man would see smoke between the sky and the earth, and a man would speak with another and hear his words but would not see him because of the smoke. Abū Sufyān and a group with him came to him (the Prophet, ﷺ), appealed to him by God and by the ties of kinship, and promised him that if he prayed for them and lifted it from them, they would believe. When he lifted it from them, they returned to their polytheism. In the same narration: The Prophet (ﷺ) had mercy on them and sent them charity and property. Also in it: When prosperity reached them, they returned to their former state, and God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿On the Day when We will seize with the greatest seizing, indeed We will take retribution﴾. He said: This means the Day of Badr.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Five have already passed: the smoke, the lazām, the seizing, the moon, and the Romans. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj said: ﴿The Day when the sky will bring forth﴾ is the Day of the Conquest of Mecca, when the dust covered the sky.

In the narration of Ḥudhayfah: The first of the signs are the emergence of the Dajjāl (the false messiah), the smoke, the descent of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, and a fire that will come out from the depth of ʿAdan. In it I said: "O Prophet of God, what is the smoke regarding this verse: ﴿So watch for the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke﴾?" He mentioned the rest of the narration, and we have summarized it.

﴿A visible smoke﴾: clearly visible. There is no doubt that it is a smoke. ﴿Covering the people﴾: it encompasses them. If it is the one Quraysh saw, then "the people" is specific to the disbelievers of Mecca, and it has already passed, as Ibn Masʿūd said. If it is among the minor signs of the Hour, or it is the Day of Resurrection, then "the people" is general to those who encounter the time of the signs, and general to all people on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿This is a painful punishment﴾ up to ﴿believers﴾ is in a position of accusative (naṣb, the grammatical case of the object) by a verb of saying that is omitted, and it is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: they will say. It is permissible that it be a report from God, as if it were an expression of amazement, as He said in the story of the sacrificed son: ﴿Indeed, this is a manifest trial﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 106].

﴿Indeed, we are believers﴾: a promise of faith if the punishment is lifted from them, and faith is obligatory whether the punishment is lifted or not.

﴿How can they have the reminder?﴾: that is, how can they be mindful, take admonition, and say what they promised of faith at the lifting of the punishment, when there has come to them what is greater? And it is included in the category of "being mindful through the lifting of the smoke"? That is what appeared at the hand of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) of signs and clear proofs, of the inimitable Book and other miracles. Yet they were not mindful, turned away from it, and slandered him by claiming that ʿAddās, a non-Arab slave of a man from Thaqīf, was the one who taught him, and they attributed him to madness. Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh recited: muʿallimun (with a kasra on the lām).

﴿Indeed, We will lift the punishment a little﴾: a report about the establishment of the proof against them, and an emphasis on granting them respite. Then He informed that they would return to disbelief. Qatādah said: It is a threat of the return in the Hereafter. If the address is to Quraysh when the drought struck them, it is clear. If the smoke is before the Day of Resurrection, then when the sky brings the punishment, their hypocrites and disbelievers will beseech and say: "Our Lord, lift the punishment from us; indeed we are believers." So He lifts it from them; it was said: after forty days. When He lifts it from them, they will apostatize. According to this view, the Day of the Great Seizing is the Day of Resurrection, like His saying: ﴿So when the Greatest Calamity comes﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 34]. That it is the Day of Resurrection is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Qatādah. That it is the Day of Badr is the view of ʿAbdullāh, Ubayy, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Mujāhid.

﴿Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you﴾: meaning not accused, God has entrusted me with His revelation and His message.

The word fakih is often used for one who is light-hearted and mocking, so it is as if they were being frivolous about the form of the blessing they were in. Al-Jawharī said: "faki­ha al-rajulu" (with a kasrah) means he is faki­h if he is a joker, and fakih also means insolent. Al-Qushayrī said: fākihīn means heedless in the same way. Al-Zajjāj said: The meaning is that the matter is thus; so one stops at "thus" (kadhālika). The kāf is in the position of the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject. It was said: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, meaning: He does a deed like that to whoever He wants to destroy. Al-Kalbī said: Thus do I do to whoever disobeys Me. Al-Ḥawfī said: We destroyed with destruction, and We took retribution with retribution, thus. Al-Zamakhsharī said: The kāf is in the accusative, meaning: like that removal, We removed them from it, ﴿and We made it an inheritance for another people﴾, who were not of them, and they are the Children of Israel. They had been enslaved in the hands of the Copts, so God destroyed the Copts at their hands and made them inherit their kingdom. Qatādah and al-Ḥasan said: the Children of Israel returned to Egypt after the destruction of Pharaoh. The view of Qatādah was judged weak, because it is not reported in the well-known histories that the Children of Israel returned to Egypt at any time from that period, nor did they ever rule it, unless Qatādah meant that they inherited its type in the lands of Syria. End of quote. But there is no weight in histories, for falsehood is abundant in them, and the speech of God is truth. He said in the sura of al-Shuʿarāʾ: ﴿Thus, and We made it an inheritance for the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 59]. It was also said: "another people" refers to those who ruled Egypt after the Copts, from other than the Children of Israel.

﴿So the heaven and earth did not weep over them﴾: this is a metaphor (istiʿārah) to belittle their affair, and that nothing changed due to their destruction. In exaltation one says: the heaven and earth wept over him, the wind wept for him, and the sun darkened for him. Zayd ibn Mufarrigh said:

The wind weeps for his grief, and the lightning flashes in its clouds.

Jarīr said:

The sun is rising, not eclipsed, weeping for you, and the stars of night and the moon.

al-Nābighah said:

Ḥārith al-Jawlān wept for the loss of his lord, and Ḥawrān, humble and bowed down, is with him.

Jarīr said:

When the pride came, the walls of the city were humbled, and the high mountains.

ويَقُولُ في التَّحْقِيرِ: ماتَ فُلانٌ، فَما خَشَعَتِ الجِبالُ.

It is said, in belittling someone: "So-and-so died, and the mountains did not humble themselves."

ونِسْبَةُ هَذِهِ الأشْياءِ لِما لا يَعْقِلُ ولا يَصِيرُ ذَلِكَ مِنهُ حَقِيقَةً، عِبارَةٌ عَنْ تَأثُّرِ النّاسِ لَهُ، أوْ عَنْ عَدَمِهِ.

Attributing these things to what has no intellect, and such (acts) not truly arising from it, is an expression of the people's being affected by him, or of their not being affected.

وقِيلَ: هو عَلى حَذْفِ مُضافٍ، أيْ: فَما بَكى عَلَيْهِمْ أهْلُ السَّماءِ وأهْلُ المَلائِكَةِ وأهْلُ الأرْضِ، وهُمُ المُؤْمِنُونَ، بَلْ كانُوا بِهَلاكِهِمْ مَسْرُورِينَ.

It has also been said that it involves an elided noun (ḥadhf muḍāf), meaning: "The people of the heavens, the people of the angels and the people of the earth did not weep over them," and they are the believers; rather, they were delighted at their destruction. This was narrated from al-Ḥasan.

وما رُوِيَ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، وابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، ومُجاهِدٍ، وابْنِ جُبَيْرٍ: إنَّ المُؤْمِنَ إذا ماتَ، بَكى عَلَيْهِ مِنَ (p-٣٧)الأرْضِ مَوْضِعُ عِبادَتِهِ أرْبَعِينَ صَباحًا، وبَكى عَلَيْهِ في السَّماءِ مَوْضِعُ صُعُودِ عَمَلِهِ. قالُوا: فَلَمْ يَكُنْ في قَوْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ مَن هَذِهِ حالُهُ تَمْثِيلٌ.

What was narrated from ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and Ibn Jubayr is that when a believer dies, the place of his worship on the earth weeps for him for forty mornings, and in the heavens the place where his deeds ascended weeps for him. They said: "Thus there was none among the people of Pharaoh whose state was this," as an illustration.

﴿وما كانُوا مُنْظَرِينَ﴾: أيْ مُؤَخَّرِينَ عَنِ العَذابِ لَمّا حانَ وقْتُ هَلاكِهِمْ، بَلْ عَجَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهم ذَلِكَ في الدُّنْيا.

﴿And they were not reprieved﴾: that is, they were not delayed from the punishment when the time of their destruction had come; rather, God hastened that for them in this world.

﴿So watch for the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke﴾. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd al-Khudrī, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and al-Ḥasan said: It is a smoke that will come on the Day of Resurrection. It will afflict the believer with something like a cold, and it will cook the heads of the disbelievers and the hypocrites, until they become like a roasted, grilled meat (miṣlaqah ḥanīdhah).

Ibn Masʿūd, Abū al-ʿĀliyah, and al-Nakhaʿī said: It is the smoke that Quraysh saw. It was said to ʿAbdullāh (Ibn Masʿūd): "A storyteller at the gates of Kinda says that it is a smoke that will come on the Day of Resurrection and will seize the breaths of the people." He said: "Whoever knows something should speak of it, and whoever does not know should say: God knows best. Now, I will tell you that when Quraysh rebelled against the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he invoked against them, saying: 'O God, tighten Your grip upon Mudar, and make it upon them years like the years of Joseph.' So hardship struck them until they ate carrion and al-ʿilhiz. Al-ʿilhiz is wool in which a tick falls, and the wool is roasted with the blood of the tick and eaten." In the same narration: "Until they ate the bones." A man would see smoke between the sky and the earth, and a man would speak with another and hear his words but would not see him because of the smoke. Abū Sufyān and a group with him came to him (the Prophet, ﷺ), appealed to him by God and by the ties of kinship, and promised him that if he prayed for them and lifted it from them, they would believe. When he lifted it from them, they returned to their polytheism. In the same narration: The Prophet (ﷺ) had mercy on them and sent them charity and property. Also in it: When prosperity reached them, they returned to their former state, and God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿On the Day when We will seize with the greatest seizing, indeed We will take retribution﴾. He said: This means the Day of Badr.

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Five have already passed: the smoke, the lazām, the seizing, the moon, and the Romans. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj said: ﴿The Day when the sky will bring forth﴾ is the Day of the Conquest of Mecca, when the dust covered the sky.

In the narration of Ḥudhayfah: The first of the signs are the emergence of the Dajjāl (the false messiah), the smoke, the descent of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, and a fire that will come out from the depth of ʿAdan. In it I said: "O Prophet of God, what is the smoke regarding this verse: ﴿So watch for the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke﴾?" He mentioned the rest of the narration, and we have summarized it.

﴿A visible smoke﴾: clearly visible. There is no doubt that it is a smoke. ﴿Covering the people﴾: it encompasses them. If it is the one Quraysh saw, then "the people" is specific to the disbelievers of Mecca, and it has already passed, as Ibn Masʿūd said. If it is among the minor signs of the Hour, or it is the Day of Resurrection, then "the people" is general to those who encounter the time of the signs, and general to all people on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿This is a painful punishment﴾ up to ﴿believers﴾ is in a position of accusative (naṣb, the grammatical case of the object) by a verb of saying that is omitted, and it is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: they will say. It is permissible that it be a report from God, as if it were an expression of amazement, as He said in the story of the sacrificed son: ﴿Indeed, this is a manifest trial﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 106].

﴿Indeed, we are believers﴾: a promise of faith if the punishment is lifted from them, and faith is obligatory whether the punishment is lifted or not.

﴿How can they have the reminder?﴾: that is, how can they be mindful, take admonition, and say what they promised of faith at the lifting of the punishment, when there has come to them what is greater? And it is included in the category of "being mindful through the lifting of the smoke"? That is what appeared at the hand of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) of signs and clear proofs, of the inimitable Book and other miracles. Yet they were not mindful, turned away from it, and slandered him by claiming that ʿAddās, a non-Arab slave of a man from Thaqīf, was the one who taught him, and they attributed him to madness. Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh recited: muʿallimun (with a kasra on the lām).

﴿Indeed, We will lift the punishment a little﴾: a report about the establishment of the proof against them, and an emphasis on granting them respite. Then He informed that they would return to disbelief. Qatādah said: It is a threat of the return in the Hereafter. If the address is to Quraysh when the drought struck them, it is clear. If the smoke is before the Day of Resurrection, then when the sky brings the punishment, their hypocrites and disbelievers will beseech and say: "Our Lord, lift the punishment from us; indeed we are believers." So He lifts it from them; it was said: after forty days. When He lifts it from them, they will apostatize. According to this view, the Day of the Great Seizing is the Day of Resurrection, like His saying: ﴿So when the Greatest Calamity comes﴾ [al-Nāziʿāt: 34]. That it is the Day of Resurrection is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Qatādah. That it is the Day of Badr is the view of ʿAbdullāh, Ubayy, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Mujāhid.

The word yawma (the object of time) in ﴿the Day We will seize﴾ is in the accusative. It was said: it is governed by their remembrance (dhikrāhum). It was said: it is governed by ﴿We will take retribution﴾, which indicates it. This was judged weak because the accusative is only governed by a verb. It was also said: it is governed by "will take retribution," and this was rebutted on the grounds that what follows inna does not govern what precedes it. Al-Jumhūr (the majority) recited nabṭishu, with a fatḥah on the nūn and a kasrah on the ṭāʾ. Al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar read it with a ḍammah on it; also al-Ḥasan, Abū Raja', and Ṭalḥah read it with a ḍammah on the nūn and a kasrah on the ṭāʾ, meaning: We will empower over them one who seizes them. The word al-baṭshata (the seizing), in this reading, is not in the accusative governed by nabṭishu, but by an implied verb, meaning: We will make that empowered one seize the seizing; or al-baṭshata means the same as al-ibṭāshah (the act of seizing), so it is in the accusative governed by nabṭishu.

﴿And We had already tested before them the people of Pharaoh﴾: this is like an example for Quraysh. The story of the one to whom Moses, peace be upon him, was sent is mentioned, and they denied him, so God destroyed them. It was also read fattannā, with a shaddah on the tāʾ, for emphasis in the verb or for multiplication, related to ... ﴿And there came to them a noble messenger﴾: meaning noble with God and with the believers, said by al-Farrāʾ; or noble in himself, because prophets are only sent from the best of people, said by Abū Sulaymān; or noble in character, good of disposition, said by Muqātil.

﴿That deliver to me the servants of God﴾: it may be that anna is explanatory (tafsīriyyah), since something preceded that indicates the meaning of saying, which is "a noble messenger." It may also be that anna is the lightened form (mukhaffafah) of the heavy (thaqīlah) anna, or the anna that governs the present verb (nāṣibah), since it is connected to the imperative. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Deliver to me obedience, O servants of God," meaning: follow me in what I call you to of faith. Mujāhid, Qatādah, and Ibn Zayd said: He asked them to deliver to him the Children of Israel, as He said: ﴿So send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them﴾ [Ṭāhā: 47]. According to the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿibāda llāh (servants of God) is a vocative, and the object of "deliver" is omitted. According to the view of Mujāhid and those mentioned with him, ʿibāda llāh is the object of "deliver."

﴿Indeed, I am a trustworthy messenger to you﴾: meaning not accused, God has entrusted me with His revelation and His message.

﴿And that you not exalt yourselves over God﴾: meaning do not be arrogant against the worship of God, said by Yaḥyā ibn Sallām. Ibn Jurayj said: Do not magnify yourselves over God. It was said: the difference between them is that magnification (taʿẓīm) is the superiority of the powerful, and arrogance (istikbār) is the elevation of one who is despised, mentioned by al-Māwardī. And anna here had the preceding one in its three aspects.

﴿Indeed, I bring you a clear authority﴾: meaning a clear proof in itself, and making clear the truth of my claim. Al-Jumhūr read innī with a kasrah on the hamzah, as a report. A group read it with a fatḥah on the hamzah. The meaning then: "Do not exalt yourselves over God because I come to you," so this is a rebuke to them, as you would say: "Do you become angry if someone tells you the truth?"

﴿And indeed, I have sought refuge﴾: meaning I have sought protection ﴿with my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me﴾. They had threatened him with death, so he sought refuge from that. It was read ʿudtu (with the vowel of the verb), with idghām (assimilation of the two identical letters). Qatādah and others said: The stoning here is with stones. Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Ṣāliḥ said: with insult. Qatādah's view is more evident, because words not befitting were said against him. This seeking of refuge was before God informed him with His saying: ﴿They will not reach you﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 35].

﴿And if you do not believe in me﴾, meaning you do not affirm me, ﴿then leave me alone﴾, meaning be apart from me. This is a good form of partnership (mushārakah), ﴿So he called upon his Lord: "Indeed, I am overpowered, so give victory"﴾ [al-Qamar: 10].

﴿That these people﴾: a word of contempt for them. Al-Jumhūr read anna hāʾulāʾi with a fatḥah on the hamzah, meaning: because these people. Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿĪsā, al-Ḥasan in one narration, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it with a kasrah.

﴿So travel with My servants﴾: there is an omission in the speech, meaning: take retribution upon them. Then God said to him: "Travel with My servants," and they are the Children of Israel and whoever among the Copts believed in him. Al-Zamakhsharī said: In it there are two aspects: the implied saying after the fāʾ, so that it is "He said: Travel with My servants," and that it is the answer to an omitted condition, as if it were said: "He said: If the matter is as you say, then travel with My servants." End of quote. This man often permits omitting the conditional clause and keeping its answer, which is not permitted except with clear evidence, such as the imperative preceding it or something similar, as mentioned in grammar, with disagreement on that.

﴿Indeed, you will be pursued﴾: meaning Pharaoh and his soldiers will pursue you, so you will be saved and the pursuers will drown.

﴿And leave the sea parted (rahwan)﴾: Ibn ʿAbbās said: still, as it was when it was parted. Mujāhid and ʿIkrimah said: dry, from His saying: ﴿So strike for them a dry path through the sea﴾ [Ṭāhā: 77]. al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: soft and smooth. ʿIkrimah said: with paths. Ibn Zayd said: easy. Mujāhid also said: separated. Qatādah said: Moses wanted to strike the sea with his staff, after he had crossed it, so that it would close back, and he feared that Pharaoh would follow him. It was said to him: "Why is this?" ﴿Indeed, they are an army to be drowned﴾: meaning in it, because when they see it still in its state when Moses and the Children of Israel entered it, or open as a dry path, they enter it, and God closes it upon them.

﴿How much they left behind﴾: meaning many things they left behind.

﴿Of gardens and springs﴾: their explanations were already mentioned in al-Shuʿarāʾ. Al-Jumhūr read wa-maqāmin (with a fatḥah on the mīm). Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Ibn Jubayr said: it means the place of standing (al-maqām). Ibn Hurmuz, Qatādah, Ibn al-Sumayfaʿ, and Nāfiʿ, in the narration of Kharijah, read it with a ḍammah. Qatādah said: it means the fine places of gatherings, dwellings, and others. Wa-naʿmatin (with a fatḥah on the nūn): the freshness of life and the sweetness of living. Abū Raja' read wa-naʿmatin in the accusative, conjoined to kam (how much): ﴿they were in it enjoying (fākihīn)﴾. Al-Jumhūr read it with an alif, meaning: those with contented souls and possessors of fruit, like Lābin and Tāmir. Abū Raja' and al-Ḥasan read it without an alif. Al-Ḥawfī said: We destroyed with destruction, and We took retribution with retribution, thus. Al-Zamakhsharī said: The kāf is in the accusative, meaning: like that removal, We removed them from it, ﴿and We made it an inheritance for another people﴾, who were not of them, and they are the Children of Israel. They had been enslaved in the hands of the Copts, so God destroyed the Copts at their hands and made them inherit their kingdom. Qatādah and al-Ḥasan said: the Children of Israel returned to Egypt after the destruction of Pharaoh. End of quote. But there is no weight in histories, for falsehood is abundant in them, and the speech of God is truth. He said in the sura of al-Shuʿarāʾ: ﴿Thus, and We made it an inheritance for the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 59]. It was also said: "another people" refers to those who ruled Egypt after the Copts, from other than the Children of Israel.
